The export takes the same filters. Pages are cut by insertion sequence, so entries that share a timestamp are never repeated or skipped; pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page. 422 invalid_time_range for a malformed from or to, and 422 for a bulk that is not a UUID. An instance admin reads every entry. An Admin of one or more environments (environments.audit) reads only the entries on those environments, or on every environment when they are Admin of all of them, never an instance-level event such as a sign-in or a settings change; the scope is applied before paging. Anyone else gets 403, audited as permission.denied with reason no_audit_scope.

post.description: Replaces everything in this Bayplan with the uploaded backup. The backup is opened, migrated to this version, re-keyed to this instance's master key and verified on a private copy first; nothing live changes until all of that has worked. Then Bayplan saves the current database as backups/prerestore-<time>.db, swaps the restored one in and restarts itself. The answer is 202 and Bayplan is unreachable for a moment; everyone is signed out, including the caller. confirm must be this instance's name (422 confirm_mismatch). The same refusals as the check apply and leave everything as it was, and 429 rate_limited when the caller has used their attempts. post.description: Does one action to up to 25 containers, each named by its node ID and container ID, and answers one result per target in request order. The actions are start, stop, restart, kill, pause and unpause. A stop or restart uses the container's own stop timeout and signal and a kill sends SIGKILL; a request with exactly one target may set timeout or signal, and a request with more is refused 422 options_single_only. Starting a running container or stopping a stopped one is answered done, and a container removed meanwhile is not_found, so repeating an action is safe. A target is routed by node ID, never by display name. A target that fails never stops the others, and nothing is retried. At most 4 calls run at once on one node and 16 targets at once overall. With more than one target (or a bulkId sent) every audit row of the request carries the same bulk detail, a UUIDv7 the server makes when the client sends none, and the response returns it. Bayplan's own server container and any agent container are protected: to stop, kill, restart or pause one, send a single-target request whose confirm is the container's name (else 422 confirmation_required, and nothing is sent); in a request with more than one target such a container is skipped with code own_container and never acted on. Start and unpause need no confirm. An action on one of them is audited before the call (stage initiated) and after it (stage completed), and a connection that drops during the call is answered done with code connection_lost and audited as stage connection_lost with result success. A node whose agent runs read-only (BAYPLAN_AGENT_READ_ONLY) is refused with host_read_only before any call; an agent that refuses by its own policy, such as one older than the server, is agent_policy_denied. Each target is audited as container.started, container.stopped, container.restarted, container.killed, container.paused or container.unpaused, with result failure and the code when it failed. Needs containers.control (Operator) on the environment.
post.summary: Start, stop, restart, kill, pause or unpause containers

post.description: Removes up to 25 containers, each named by its node ID and container ID, and answers one result per target in request order, as the actions route does. A running container is refused with container_running unless force is true, and nothing is sent for it. Named volumes are never removed. removeVolumes also removes the container's anonymous volumes, and needs the delete volumes permission on top of containers.remove: a caller without it is refused 403 before any call and the refusal is audited as permission.denied. Bayplan's own server container and any agent container are protected: to remove one, send a single-target request whose confirm is the container's name (else 422 confirmation_required, and nothing is sent); in a request with more than one target such a container is skipped with code own_container and never acted on. Start and unpause need no confirm. An action on one of them is audited before the call (stage initiated) and after it (stage completed), and a connection that drops during the call is answered done with code connection_lost and audited as stage connection_lost with result success. Each target is audited as container.removed with its force and volumes choices. Needs containers.remove (Operator) on the environment.

get.description: Up to tail lines of the container's log that were written before until, oldest first, for "Load earlier lines". It does not follow the log. until is an RFC 3339 time or Unix seconds and is exclusive; leave it out for the newest lines. since, when given, is the earliest time to look back to. startOfLogs is true when fewer than tail lines came back because the log has no more, and false when more may be earlier (including when the page was cut to a size limit, newest lines kept). The container lives on one node, named by nodeId, with the same rules and problems as the container detail route (422 node_required, 404 container_not_found, 503 node_unavailable). sid is the viewer's ID, the one its live stream uses: a viewer is audited once however many pages it reads. The spec is decoded strictly, the host-escalation policy runs on the whole of it, the image is required and resolved to its digest (a failed lookup is 422 image_unresolved and nothing is created), and one create is sent with the registry credential and without the engine's own registry lookup. The networks, secrets and configs in objects are created first, networks then secrets then configs, their IDs are written into the spec's references, and then the service is created; each is audited as network.created, secret.created or config.created with source service_apply, never with a value. If the service cannot be created, every object this request made is removed again in reverse order (audited with source service_apply_cleanup); the problem's detail says so and its errors carry the reason on its own (location reason) and the objects as removed and notRemoved, each as kind:name. Also 422 objects_missing for a network, secret or config the spec names that does not exist and was not sent in objects, 422 spec_rejected, with Docker's words, for a spec Docker refuses, 422 too_many_objects for more than 16 objects, 422 object_duplicate for the same kind and name twice, the name, value, labels, templating and subnet problems of the secrets, configs and networks routes for a bad object, 409 name_taken when an object's name exists already, and 403 object_permission, before anything is created, for a caller without networks.manage, secrets.manage or configs.manage for a kind it would create. Problems, all before anything is created: 409 service_name_taken for a name a service has; 422 image_required for no image; 422 name_invalid for a name that is not 1 to 63 letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore; 422 spec_invalid (the decoder's message) for a spec that does not decode strictly into a swarm service spec, or for a secret reference whose SecretName is not the name of the secret its SecretID points at; 422 placeholder_unmatched for a <hidden> in the spec; 422 stack_label_reserved for a com.docker.stack. label; 422 image_unresolved when the tag cannot be resolved to a digest (a new service is never created unpinned); 409 not_a_swarm for a standalone host; 403 privileged_service, with each finding in errors, when the caller is below env Admin and the spec asks for host access. No answer, error or audit row carries a value of the environment, the command line, the health check or the log options for a caller without secrets.reveal, or the value of a staged secret or config. post.description: Judges a full service spec and answers what an apply would do, without changing Docker. The spec is read fresh against the service: the values a caller without secrets.reveal could not see (<hidden>) are merged back in, a changed tag is resolved to its digest through the manager with the stored registry credential (a failed lookup is imageError, and the spec stays unpinned), and the host-escalation policy runs on the decoded spec an apply would forward. The answer is the merged, normalised spec (masked again for a caller without secrets.reveal), the image, the findings, whether the caller may have them (allowed) and the networks the spec names that do not exist (missing). A refusal by the policy is not an error here: allowed is false and refusal lists the findings. Problems, all before anything is sent: 409 service_changed when the version is not the current one; 409 stack_owned for a service a stack owns; 404 service_not_found; 409 not_a_swarm for a standalone host; 422 spec_invalid (the decoder's message) for a spec that does not decode strictly into a swarm service spec, or for a secret reference whose SecretName is not the name of the secret its SecretID points at, whoever sends it; 422 placeholder_unmatched for a <hidden> with no current value behind it; 422 placeholder_reserved when a caller who may reveal secrets sends <hidden>; 422 name_immutable and 422 mode_immutable for a changed name or kind of mode; 422 stack_label_reserved for a com.docker.stack. label the service did not have; 403 privileged_service, with each finding in errors, when a caller below env Admin sends host access (a bind outside /srv, /mnt and /media or of a runtime socket, a local volume that binds a relative host path or one outside those roots, or mounts a filesystem type other than tmpfs or a network share, a named pipe, an added capability, SELinux disabled or spc_t, seccomp unconfined or custom, AppArmor disabled, the host network, a plugin runtime). 403 secret_reveal_required, with each added reference in errors, when a caller without secrets.reveal adds a secret the service does not use (compared by the engine's secret ID, a name being resolved through the swarm's secret list); Needs services.control (Operator) on the environment. post.description: Takes a revision from the draft and deploys it as a job, answering 202 with the job ID at once; the deploy goes on if the browser closes. draftVersion must be the version of the draft you reviewed, or the answer is 409 draft_changed. A draft that started from an older revision than the newest good one (someone deployed since) is 409 concurrent_unacknowledged unless acknowledgeConcurrent is true; a deploy never overwrites a newer one unseen. pins, when sent, are the review's: the deploy uses exactly those digests and makes no registry lookup (422 pins_invalid for one the server would not have chosen). On a standalone host the job checks the stack, pins each image the same way (a service that runs the text it is deployed with keeps its digest; a new or changed one is looked up on the host with the stored credential), pulls each image of a container it will create or recreate that the host does not have, with the stored credential and never the SDK's anonymous pull (a Pull step under the lookup with the bytes done of the total; a refused pull ends it with its pull_denied, pull_unauthorized, image_not_found, rate_limited or registry_tls code and nothing is created), and runs the Compose SDK's up over a guarded client: containers created, those whose configuration changed recreated, the others left alone, those of services the file no longer declares removed, and a wait until they run; they carry com.docker.compose.project and bayplan.stack.id, and bayplan.stack.image holds the image as written. A stack secret or config is written into the container, not mounted from a file. On a swarm the job checks the stack, looks up each image and pins it to a digest (the one the service runs, or a fresh lookup through a manager), creates the stack's networks, then its secrets and configs under names that end in a short hash of their content, then its services, through one manager, each once and never retried; each carries com.docker.stack.namespace and bayplan.stack.id, and each service com.docker.stack.image with the image as written. A service is done when it converges, not when the swarm took it: the job polls each service every 2 seconds, up to BAYPLAN_STACK_CONVERGE_TIMEOUT (10 minutes by default), until its tasks run on its current spec and its update completed. A secret or config that content changes replaces is removed at the end, once every service uses the new one. A compose file that does not load is 422 compose_invalid; one that uses a setting a swarm can't deploy at all is 422 compose_unsupported; one whose check finds an error is 422 stack_invalid. A caller below env Admin is refused 403 privileged_compose, with each setting and its line in errors, when the stack asks for host access (a bind of the Docker socket or a host path outside /srv, /mnt and /media, an added capability, privileged, the host network, a device), judged on the values of the stack's variables. A name that something Bayplan does not manage holds (a swarm namespace or a Compose project) is 409 stack_name_clash. An environment that is no longer the kind of target the stack was created for is 409 target_changed. At most 5 jobs of one user run at once (429 too_many_deploys). Only one stack operation at a time runs on an environment: while one does, on any stack, a deploy is refused 409 operation_locked with errors naming the stack, the job and when it started, and nothing is stored. Just before it writes anything the job judges the host access of the stack again for the caller, so a grant removed since the request still stops it (the check step fails needs_admin). With mode update, only the services named in services take a newly looked-up digest (the ones the review chose, sent as pins) and every other service keeps the digest it runs; a request that names no service, or one the stack does not have, is 422 services_invalid and nothing is stored. Writes one stack.deployed audit row, with the mode and the result, when the job ends. Needs stacks.deploy (Operator).

A stopped stack is state stopped, and a stack with no revision that deployed is not_deployed. The newest check is answered unless fresh is true or there is none; callers that ask for a fresh check of one stack at the same moment share one read. Nothing is changed on any engine. The answer holds the live settings of running services, so for a caller without secrets.reveal on the environment every environment value, command, argument, health check command and log option is <hidden>, and a setting that differs only in such a value is listed by its path in hiddenChanges, with no value. Objects the deployed compose file refers to that were made outside the stack are listed with ownership external. A standalone stack's secrets and configs are read from its deployed definition, because they are files in the containers. Each card is read on its own and carries its own error (a code, never the engine's text), so one read that fails never hides the others. No secret value and no config content is read. A stack ID of another environment is 404 stack_not_found. Needs stacks.read (Viewer).

post.description: Reviews the stack's saved draft (the latest good revision when there is no draft) against what is running and saves nothing. It runs the same check as the editor, looks up the digests of the images that need one, converts the stack the way a deploy does, reads what the swarm holds under the stack's namespace and answers the problems, a summary, an image table, each service's change with its masked current and next spec, and the other resources. A value derived from a secret of the stack is <hidden> on both sides; whether it changed is decided before it is hidden and listed in hiddenChanges as a path. Right after a deploy, a review shows no change. yaml is the one comparison with the last deploy and not with what is running: the rendered stack against the masked rendering stored with the last good revision, as hunks computed here with 3 lines of context. concurrent is set when someone deployed after the draft was started, with what that deployment changed and what the draft changed, file by file; the deploy then needs acknowledgeConcurrent. Send the answer's draftVersion and pins with the deploy, and the deploy uses exactly these digests. For a caller below env Admin, host access (a bind of the Docker socket or of a host path outside /srv, /mnt and /media, an added capability, privileged, the host network, a device), judged on the values of the stack's variables, is a blocking needs_admin problem at its line, and needsAdmin names the kinds. A name that something Bayplan does not manage holds is a blocking stack_name_clash problem, and another stack operation running on the environment is a blocking operation_locked problem. On a standalone host the review pins the images the same way and compares each service with the containers that run it: the service a deploy would send, and the service rebuilt from each running container's inspect document, both with what the image or the engine fills in taken out, so that right after a deploy nothing differs. A service with no container is added; one whose containers carry another config hash than the service has now, or whose running configuration is not what the file says (a container changed by hand on the host, which keeps its labels and its hash), is changed, with the masked current and next settings as compose settings (restart, ports, environment, volumes ...); a changed secret or config is a changed service; and a service of the host's Compose project that the file no longer declares is removed. Settings the engine does not record (depends_on, secrets, configs, profiles, pull_policy) are read from the stored revision that made the container, and are the file's own when none did. A deploy that recreates a service carries others with it, as docker compose does: a service that shares its network, IPC or PID namespace or its volumes is recreated and keeps its pinned image, and one that depends on it with restart: true is stopped and started again; they follow as recreated and restarted rows with because naming the service, carry no spec, and are not counted in the summary. A container changed by hand is put right by a deploy of an unedited file. An environment that is no longer the kind of target the stack was created for is 409 target_changed. In mode update, only the services named in services look their tag up again and every other service keeps the digest it runs; each row of images then carries the digest it runs now in current and the one it would run in digest, and a tag that did not move reads pinned with the note Already up to date. A request that names no service, or one the stack does not have, is 422 services_invalid and nothing is looked up. In mode rollback, revision names the revision to restore (422 revision_required without it, 404 revision_not_found for one the stack does not hold, 409 revision_not_good for one that did not end good). The review is of that revision, not of the draft: it is converted, judged for host access for the caller and compared with the services, networks, secrets and configs that run now, with each image set to the digest the revision stored (state pinned, note revision), and no registry is asked. yaml is the revision's rendering against the deployed revision's, and concurrent is never set. deployedSeq is the newest good revision's number, to send as expectedDeployed. On a standalone host the revision is compared with the host's containers by config hash and field diff, as a draft's review is, with each image set to the reference the revision stored; a network or volume a later revision added stays on the host and is not listed. A revision that cannot be redeployed as it stands is one blocking revision_not_deployable problem. Needs stacks.deploy (Operator).
post.summary: Review what a deploy of a stack would do

get.description: Every deploy of the stack is a revision. They come newest first by revision number, with how each came to be (origin), the revision a roll back copied, the result (outcome, and for a failed one the service and the sentence of its failure code), who started it and when, and the images that changed against the next older good revision. The newest good revision is marked deployed. Only references, codes and names are listed: no file, variable or rendered text. A stack with no revision answers an empty list. A stack ID of another environment is 404 stack_not_found. Needs stacks.read (Viewer).
get.summary: The revisions of a stack

get.description: What a revision deployed: the rendering stored with it, its files (path and whether secret; a file's content is never sent), its variables (a secret variable's value is <hidden>, for every caller: there is no reveal for a revision), the images it pinned by service with their digests, and the difference of its rendering from the deployed revision's. A revision number the stack does not hold (never taken, or deleted by retention) is 404 revision_not_found; a stack ID of another environment is 404 stack_not_found. Needs stacks.read (Viewer).
get.summary: One revision of a stack

get.description: The services a roll back to the revision would add, change or remove against what is running now, the same comparison the roll back review makes (the revision converted with the digests it stored, no registry asked). Only a revision that ended good qualifies: a pending or failed one is 409 revision_not_good, a number the stack does not hold is 404 revision_not_found, and a stack ID of another environment is 404 stack_not_found. A revision that can no longer be redeployed is 409 revision_not_deployable. The answer holds the live settings of running services, so for a caller without secrets.reveal on the environment every environment value, command, argument, health check command and log option is <hidden>, and a setting that differs only in such a value is listed by its path in hiddenChanges, with no value. One user may have two of these reads running; a third is 429 check_busy. Needs stacks.read (Viewer).
get.summary: What rolling back to a revision would change

post.description: Redeploys a revision of the stack that ran well, as a job, answering 202 with the job ID at once. With no body, that is the newest revision whose deploy succeeded, or, when the newest revision is itself the one that runs, the good one before it. With revision, it is that one: any revision whose deploy ended good, the deployed one included (useful after a newer attempt failed). A revision that failed or is still deploying is 409 revision_not_good; one the stack does not hold is 404 revision_not_found. expectedDeployed is the number of the deployed revision the review was made against; if the stack was deployed again since, the answer is 409 deployed_changed and nothing is stored. It takes a revision of its own from it (the files, the variables and the images it ran, recorded as origin rollback with restored_from naming the revision it restored) and runs the same swarm deploy on it, so it is audited as stack.deployed with the mode rollback, the revision and restoredFrom. It uses exactly the images that revision ran and looks nothing up: a tag that has moved since is not followed. The draft is not touched. A stack with no earlier version that ran well is 409 no_previous_version. Everything a deploy is judged on is judged again: a revision that uses host access is refused 403 privileged_compose below env Admin, a stack that no longer loads is 422, and while another stack operation runs on the environment the answer is 409 operation_locked and nothing is stored. A stack of a standalone host rolls back the same way, through the Compose SDK: the containers whose configuration differs are recreated from the images the revision stored, networks and volumes a later revision added stay on the host, and the foreign-project check is made before anything is written. A roll back is only ever sent by a person; nothing rolls a stack back by itself. Needs stacks.deploy (Operator).
post.summary: Roll a stack back to a revision that ran well

get.description: The services the stack owns on the engine, read now: on a swarm each service with its task counts, its image as written and as pinned and its published ports; on a standalone host each service with its containers. A service the engine holds under the stack's name that Bayplan did not make is not listed. A stack that was never deployed answers an empty list. A stack ID of another environment is 404 stack_not_found. An environment that cannot be read is the environment's own problem answer. Needs stacks.read (Viewer).
get.summary: What a stack runs now

post.description: Brings a stopped stack back as a job, answering 202 with the job ID and whether it recreates services. It brings back the last version that was deployed, never the saved draft and never a newer image: on a swarm each service is scaled back to the count it remembered and the label removed, and a service a stop removed is created again from the last good revision with the image digest it ran; on a standalone host the Compose SDK starts the stopped containers and a stack file's secrets and configs are written into each again before it starts. A start that creates services is judged by the host-access policy for the caller, as a deploy is: below env Admin it is refused 403 privileged_compose when the revision uses host access. A stack that is not stopped is 409 not_stopped. While another stack operation runs on the environment the answer is 409 operation_locked and nothing is stored. Writes one stack.started audit row when the job ends. Needs stacks.deploy (Operator).
post.summary: Start a stopped stack

post.description: Parks the stack as a job, answering 202 with the job ID at once. On a swarm every replicated service is scaled to 0 and its count is remembered in the service-level label bayplan.stack.stopped-replicas (the label is not part of the task template, so no task is replaced), and the global and job services are removed. On a standalone host the Compose SDK stops the stack's containers. Networks, volumes, secrets and configs are never removed. The stack is marked stopped once everything has stopped; a stop that fails stops where it failed and what already stopped stays stopped. A stack that is stopped already, was never deployed or has nothing running is 409 nothing_running. Only one stack operation at a time runs on an environment: while one does, the answer is 409 operation_locked naming it and nothing is stored. Writes one stack.stopped audit row when the job ends. Needs stacks.deploy (Operator).
post.summary: Stop a stack

post.description: Answers the saved value of a secret variable of the stack, in clear: the one way back to a value every other answer shows as <hidden>. The value is read from the saved draft, or from the last deployed definition when there is no draft. A variable that is not in it, is not secret or has no value is 404 variable_not_found. The answer is never cached. Every reveal is audited as stack.value_revealed with the stack, the kind (variable) and the name, never the value; if the audit row cannot be written the value is not sent. A refusal is audited as permission.denied. Needs secrets.reveal (Admin, or an Operator granted the extra).

post.description: Takes over a swarm namespace or a Compose project that Bayplan does not manage. Bayplan reads what runs, rebuilds the compose definition itself (the body carries none), and in one transaction stores the stack (source adopted), its draft and revision 1 (origin adopted, good, pinned to the images that run). Nothing is sent to any engine: the stack's objects get Bayplan's labels on its first deploy. The definition holds the environment values as literals. The fingerprint is the one the stack's page read; when what runs has changed since, the answer is 409 adopt_stale and nothing is stored. Adopting never fails on the host-access policy: it only records what already runs. With source paste the definition is the original compose file in compose instead (the person still has it): it is checked again here by the same check as any draft and never trusted from the page, stored exactly as written (comments and key order kept) as the draft and revision 1 together with vars (a secret one sealed), pinned to the digests that run for the services that run; a file that does not pass is 422 pasted_file_invalid. A stack that is Bayplan's own, runs Bayplan's agent, or has a name its target cannot hold is 409 stack_not_adoptable with the reason; a name Bayplan already manages is 409 stack_already_managed with the stack's ID in errors as stackId; a name nothing carries is 404 unmanaged_stack_not_found; a stack that cannot be written as a compose file that passes the check is 422 rebuild_failed. Only one stack operation at a time runs on an environment: while one does, the answer is 409 operation_locked and nothing is stored. Answers the stack, as the stack route does. Audited as stack.adopted. Needs stacks.create (Env Admin).

It reads the engine and changes nothing, on the engine or in the store, and a gap never blocks adopting. The fingerprint it answers is the one to send with the adoption. With source paste the body carries the original compose file and its variables instead: the file goes through the same check as any draft (no include, no extends, no file read from the server, at most 1 MiB) and is compared with what runs; a file with an error answers blocked true with its problems and nothing compared, and matches says it differs from what runs in nothing but the ownership labels. The answer holds the live settings of running services, so for a caller without secrets.reveal on the environment every environment value, command, argument, health check command and log option is <hidden>. A stack that is Bayplan's own, runs Bayplan's agent, or has a name its target cannot hold is 409 stack_not_adoptable; a name Bayplan already manages is 409 stack_already_managed with the stack's ID in errors as stackId; a name nothing carries is 404 unmanaged_stack_not_found; a stack that cannot be written as a compose file that passes the check is 422 rebuild_failed. post.description: Creates a volume on one node, once and never retried. Volumes are node-local: nodeId names the node (the nodeId of a row of a list) and may be left out only on an environment of one node that is not a swarm (else 422 node_required). The driver is local unless one is named. 409 name_taken when the node already has a volume of that name (the engine would silently reuse it), 409 host_read_only on a read-only host, 409 agent_host_policy when the node's agent refuses a volume that mounts a host folder outside /srv, /mnt and /media, mounts a device or uses a volume plugin, because its owner did not set BAYPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_PRIVILEGED_SERVICES=true, 503 node_unavailable when the node is not a connected node of the environment. Needs volumes.create (Admin) on the environment. Every attempt is audited as volume.created, with result failure and the code when it was refused. The audit row carries the driver option names and values with any password-like part replaced.

post.description: Deletes up to 25 volumes, each named by its node ID and name, and answers one result per target in request order. This is irreversible: the data in the volume is gone. The caller types the confirmation: the volume's name for a single target, or delete {n} volumes for several, where n is at least the number of targets in the request (else 422 confirmation_required and nothing is sent). Volumes are node-local: a volume is deleted on the node named, and the same name on another node is left alone. A volume that any container on its node, running or stopped, or any swarm service mounts is never deleted: the result is failed with code volume_in_use and the detail names up to 5 users. The users are read again from the node and from a manager just before each removal, and force is never sent, so a container that mounts the volume between the check and the call makes the engine refuse and is answered volume_in_use too. A volume the node does not have is failed with code not_found. One that fails never stops the others. Needs volumes.delete (an Operator or above with the delete volumes permission) on the environment; a caller without it is refused 403 and the refusal is audited as permission.denied. With more than one target (or a bulkId sent) every audit row of the request carries the same bulk detail, a UUIDv7 the server makes when the client sends none, and the response returns it. Every attempt on a volume that exists is audited as volume.removed, failures included.

This makes the engine walk every volume's files, which can take long on a host with large volumes, so the SPA asks only when the user presses Calculate sizes and never on a timer. At most 4 nodes calculate at once, each for at most 60 seconds; a node that fails or runs out of time answers ok false with an error, and the others are unaffected. A volume's size is -1 when the engine cannot say. 503 node_unavailable when nodeId is not a connected node of the environment. Needs volumes.read (Viewer) on the environment.

post.description: kind local is the admin's explicit opt-in to managing the Docker host Bayplan runs on (D-19): nothing is added at startup. Needs a Docker socket that answers. 409 socket_not_found, engine_unreachable, unsupported_engine (unless allowUnsupported) or local_environment_exists. kind agent creates an environment for hosts that run the Bayplan agent, with its own certificate authority and a join token, and answers install with the token (shown once) and the swarm and standalone install commands and files, built from the address agents dial (the agent URL, else the public URL, with its base path); 409 public_url_required when Bayplan has neither, and 409 insecure_agent_url when that address is plain ws:// for a host that is not this machine and BAYPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_INSECURE is off. Nothing is created in either case. 422 invalid_name. The name defaults to the hostname the daemon, or the first agent, reports. Needs environments.create. Audited as environment.added.

This lists the ones that tried in the last 24 hours, newest first, from memory: it is empty after a restart until they try again, and an agent drops off 24 hours after it stops trying. Each is reinstalled with its environment's install command. Needs environments.token (instance admin).

get.description: Derived from live state, never stored, so an item is there exactly while its cause is and cannot be dismissed: an environment that is offline (env_offline, with since and reason), a certificate that is not renewing or has expired (cert_not_renewing), agents that need an update by hand (manual_update_needed, one item with a count), a clock that is out of step (clock_skew), an environment still waiting for its first agent after 7 days (pending_long), a swarm that was re-initialised (cluster_changed) and a local host that can be folded into a swarm environment it manages (fold_offered, only for callers who hold environments.manage) and a swarm service whose tasks keep failing (restart_loop, one item per service that is not muted, only for callers who hold services.read on that environment; with service, serviceId, count, windowMinutes, latestError and since) and a standalone container that keeps dying (restart_loop_container, one item per container that is not muted, only for callers who hold containers.read on that environment; with container, containerId, nodeId, count, windowMinutes, lastExitCode and since). Only environments the caller holds environments.read for are considered, so the list never reveals what the caller cannot open, and the counts are over that set. A revoked environment says nothing here. Errors come first, then the newest. Names are at most 64 characters.

delete.description: Needs environments.delete. Stops managing the host. Revokes every agent, disables the join token and deletes the environment, and changes nothing in Docker: its containers, networks and volumes are untouched (D-20, D-30). With uninstallAgents=true each online agent is first told to uninstall itself (a swarm's agents through one manager, which removes the agent service and its token secret; every agent removes its own container and state volume), and the request waits up to 30 seconds for their answers. Whatever they answer, or do not, the revoking and deletion follow, so hosts that were offline or refused keep their agent until the admin runs the manual cleanup command that GET /api/env/{envId}/agents gives. Audited as environment.removed, agent.revoked per agent, and agent.uninstalled per agent that confirmed.

Nodes that had finished keep the image and stay done. The job ends cancelled when no node finished and partial otherwise, and the answer is the job as it stands, normally already ended. Only the user who started the pull, or a holder of images.pull on the pull's environment, may cancel it: anyone else who may not see the pull gets 404 pull_not_found, and one who sees it but cannot cancel gets 403 (audited as permission.denied). A pull that has already ended answers 409 pull_finished and nothing changes, so cancelling twice is safe. A cancel is a change and is never retried.

post.description: Stores a sign-in for a registry host and an optional namespace, used for pulls and tag browsing on every environment. The secret is sealed with the vault, included in backups and re-wrapped by key rotation, and never returned by any route afterwards: the answer carries only its last 4 characters, and only for a secret of 12 or more characters. Needs registries.instance, which only instance admins hold. 422 validation_failed names every field at fault with a stable code (name_required, name_invalid, type_invalid, host_required, host_invalid, prefix_invalid, username_required, secret_required, hub_prefix_required, hub_fallback_not_hub, expiry_invalid, expiry_past, ca_invalid); 409 credential_name_taken, host_prefix_taken or hub_fallback_taken when another instance credential clashes; the 409 names that credential in its errors list (location conflict.credential). Audited as registry.credential_created without the secret.
post.summary: Add an instance registry credential

get.description: Derived from live state, never stored, so an item is there exactly while its cause is: a credential that expires within 7 days (expiring), whose expiry day has passed (expired) or that its registry refused on the last use and that has not worked since (auth_failed). An expiry day counts as the end of that day in UTC, and the 7-day warning and expired use that same instant. Only credentials the caller may manage are listed: an instance admin gets instance and environment credentials, an Env Admin the credentials of the environments they administer, and everyone else an empty list. A credential with several problems has one item, the most severe. Nothing is renewed automatically.
get.summary: List the registry credentials that need attention

get.description: Lists a repository's tag names through the server, with the stored credential pulls would use for it among the ones the caller may see: the instance credentials and, with envId, that environment's own. The tags come newest version first and then by name, descending, 100 to a page (page, from 0), filtered by the text q and without signature, attestation and cache tags unless hide is false. The answer names the credential, never holds it, and is cached for a minute per credential, so a caller never gets a list fetched with a credential they cannot use. Needs images.read on at least one environment, and on envId when it is given (403). An unparsable reference is 422 ref_invalid. At most 60 tag requests a minute per user (a burst of 30), lists and details together: 429 rate_limited. When the registry cannot list the tags the answer is 404 repository_not_found or repository_unavailable (the registry refused the repository although the credential's sign-in works, so it does not exist or the account cannot read it), or 502 with the problem type needs_login (the registry wants a login and no stored credential matches), login_refused (it refused the matching credential), registry_unreachable or registry_tls; errors names the registry as registry.host and registry.repo and the credential used, if any, as credential.id, credential.name, credential.scopeKind and credential.scopeName. Not audited.

post.description: Reads the digest, the created date and the platforms of up to 25 tags of a repository, for the rows the person can see. The server asks the registry with the same credential and the same authorisation as the tag list: images.read on at least one environment, and on envId when it is given (403, audited), an unparsable reference is 422 ref_invalid, the limit of the tag list applies (429 rate_limited), 26 tags are 422 and so is a tag that is not 1 to 128 letters, digits, underscores, dots or dashes (tag_invalid). Docker Hub is read through its tags API, which costs no pulls; any other registry through a manifest HEAD and, per digest, the manifest and the config of one platform (linux/amd64, else the environment's node architecture, else the first). Results are cached per credential, repository and digest. A tag that could not be read carries a code, never a failure of the request. Not audited.
post.summary: Read the digest, date and platforms of tags

post.description: Runs the registry's own flow from the Bayplan server in three steps and reports each one: whether the registry answers, whether it accepts the sign-in, and, when a test repository is given, whether the sign-in can read it. Works on values that are not saved. A 401 to the unauthenticated ping counts as reachable; a refused sign-in is reported as refused whether the registry says 401 or 403; a registry that asks for no login reports signed in as not_checked. Each step is a state and a code, never text from the registry. The server refuses link-local, unspecified and multicast addresses (cloud metadata included) after DNS, allows private and loopback ranges, and refuses redirects to plain HTTP or local URLs. Needs registries.instance. At most 10 tests a minute per user across both families: 429 rate_limited. 422 validation_failed names the fields at fault with the codes of adding a credential, ca_invalid and test_repository_invalid. caPem and insecure apply the credential's own CA and switch to this test only; the operator's BAYPLAN_REGISTRY_BLOCK_CIDRS ranges stay refused even with the switch on. A stored credential's secret is lent only to the host, type, username, CA and insecure switch it was stored with: a test that changes any of them needs a secret typed now (422 secret_required). Audited as registry.credential_tested with each step's result, never the secret.
post.summary: Test a registry sign-in from the server

post.description: Asks one node of the environment envId to read the manifest of repository:tag (latest when left out) from the credential's registry with the credential, through its agent and its own engine. A firewall, an internal DNS name or a certificate authority that only the node has shows up here and cannot show up in the server's own test. The engine reads the manifest with a HEAD, which Docker Hub does not count as a pull. On a swarm the check runs on one connected manager, else on the one node; the answer names the node. Works on values that are not saved, or on a stored instance credential (credentialId). The answer is 200 whether the node could pull or not: state is passed or failed, and a failed one carries a code (pull_denied, pull_unauthorized, image_not_found, registry_unreachable, registry_tls, registry_http, rate_limited, pull_failed, agent_policy_denied when the node's agent is older than this server, node_unavailable when the node did not answer), never any text from the registry. Needs registries.instance. 422 repository_required without a repository; 422 validation_failed names the other fields at fault (tag_invalid, test_repository_invalid and those of adding a credential); 404 environment_not_found; 503 node_unavailable when no node of the environment is connected; 502 agent_policy_denied when the environment cannot be read. The 10 tests a minute per user are shared with the server tests: 429 rate_limited. The stored secret is lent only to the host, type, username, CA and insecure switch it was stored with (422 secret_required otherwise). A host that is, or resolves on the server to, an address the server's egress policy refuses (cloud metadata, link-local, BAYPLAN_REGISTRY_BLOCK_CIDRS) is not sent to the node: the answer is failed with registry_unreachable. Audited as registry.credential_tested with the environment, the node and via env, never the secret.
post.summary: Test a registry sign-in from an environment's node

delete.description: Removes the credential and its sealed secret. Pulls it would have matched fall back to the next matching credential, or to anonymous; nothing else refers to it. Needs registries.instance. A credential that is already gone, and one of an environment, answer 404 credential_not_found, so a repeated delete is safe and writes nothing. Audited as registry.credential_deleted without the secret.

get.description: The credential as the list shows it. One the caller may not see answers exactly like one that does not exist: 404 credential_not_found.
get.summary: Read one registry credential

patch.description: Changes the members that are sent and keeps the rest. The secret is write-only: leave it out or send it empty to keep the stored one, which is neither read nor returned; send a new one and it is sealed again and replaces it, and the answer carries only its last 4 characters (12 or more characters). Leaving it out keeps the stored one only while the host, type, username, CA and insecure switch stay as stored: changing any of them needs a secret typed now (422 validation_failed, secret_required on body.secret), so the stored secret never goes to a destination it was not stored for. There is no scope: a credential never moves between layers. Needs registries.instance. A credential of an environment answers 404 credential_not_found here, exactly like one that does not exist. 422 validation_failed names every field at fault with the same codes as adding; 409 credential_name_taken, host_prefix_taken or hub_fallback_taken when another instance credential clashes, naming it in its errors list (location conflict.credential). Audited as registry.credential_updated with a changed detail listing the names of the fields that changed, the secret only as the word secret, and host_from and host_to when the host changed.

get.description: publicUrlLocked is true when the BAYPLAN_PUBLIC_URL environment variable fixes the public URL (D-04), agentUrlLocked when BAYPLAN_AGENT_URL fixes the agent URL (D-18). agentEndpoint is the address agents dial: the agent URL, else the public URL, with its path and /agent/connect. enrolledAgents counts the agents that are not revoked and offlineAgents those of them with no connection now (D-19). agentEndpointRefused is true when agentEndpoint is plain ws:// for a host that is not this machine and BAYPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_INSECURE is off: agents cannot connect to it (G-02-R4-3).
get.summary: Get the instance name, public URL and agent URL

patch.description: Only the fields sent are changed. Invalid fields answer 422 with a stable code per field (instance_name_required, instance_name_too_long, invalid_public_url, invalid_agent_url, insecure_agent_url). An agent URL that is plain http for a host that is not this machine answers 422 insecure_agent_url unless BAYPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_INSECURE is on, because agents refuse such an address; a loopback or https agent URL, clearing it, and an http public URL are accepted. A different public URL while BAYPLAN_PUBLIC_URL is set answers 409 public_url_locked, and a different agent URL while BAYPLAN_AGENT_URL is set answers 409 agent_url_locked; both change nothing. An empty agentUrl clears it. A change takes effect at once: the Origin check and the cookie Secure flag use the new public URL from the next request. When the address agents dial changes, every agent connected over a TLS-verified session is sent the new address and the server's pins over its tunnel and dials that address from its next connection; an agent takes only a wss:// address this way. From then on the server accepts agent handshakes only for the new host and port, with no fallback period: an agent that was offline or on plain ws:// at the time is refused auth_rejected until it is reinstalled with the new address or the change is reverted. Each change is audited as settings.updated with the old and new value of every changed field.
patch.summary: Change the instance name, the public URL or the agent URL

delete.description: Turns the user into a tombstone and cannot be undone: they are disabled, their password, email and display name are cleared, instance admin is turned off, and their sessions, links, direct access and team memberships are removed in one step. Their username stays reserved, so creating it again answers 409 username_reserved. The automations they own pause as owner deleted, except those listed in the optional reassign body, which go to the user named for each in the same step; a user who could not run one answers 422 owner_not_eligible, one that is not the deleted user's answers 404 automation_not_found, and nothing is deleted. The last active instance admin cannot be deleted: 409 last_instance_admin. A user who is already deleted answers 404 user_not_found.

get.description: The user as the user page shows them. An unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found.
get.summary: Read one user

patch.description: Send displayName, email or both, with the updatedAt you read. If the user changed since, nothing is saved and the answer is 409 stale_change. The username can never be changed and is not accepted. An invalid field answers 422 on body.displayName or body.email. Saving what is already there changes nothing.
patch.summary: Edit a user's display name and email

get.description: The user's effective access: for each environment the user can reach, the highest role any source gives, the union of the extra permissions and every source (instance, all, team, direct), computed by the same evaluator that enforces access. An instance admin holds every environment, so the list is empty and instanceAdmin is true. grants lists the user's own grants, the ones editable on the user page. An unknown user answers 404 user_not_found.
get.summary: What a user may do on each environment, and why

post.description: Ends every session of the user at once and refuses their sign-in. Their grants and team memberships are kept and the automations they own pause. Answers the user as they now are. Disabling a disabled user changes nothing. The last active instance admin cannot be disabled: 409 last_instance_admin.
post.summary: Disable a user

post.description: Lets a disabled user sign in again with the grants and teams they had. Enabling an enabled user changes nothing.
post.summary: Enable a user

put.description: Gives the user Admin, Operator or Viewer on one environment (scope env, with envId) or on all of them (scope all). A user holds at most one grant per scope: saving an existing combination edits it (200, audited as access.updated), a new one is created (201, access.granted). Extras are accepted only on Operator: a Viewer answers 422 viewer_cannot_have_extras, an Admin 422 extras_implied and a permission that is not an extra 422 unknown_extra. With expected set, a grant that has changed answers 409 stale_change. A grant never expires. An unknown user answers 404 user_not_found and an unknown environment 404 environment_not_found.
put.summary: Give a user a role on an environment

delete.description: Removes the grant. The user loses the access it gave on their next request and keeps every other grant, and the automations they own that no longer qualify pause. The answer lists who lost which access, worked out inside the same step. Audited as one access.revoked entry carrying the subject, role, scope, impact_count and impact. A grant that is not the user's answers 404 grant_not_found.

post.description: Works out, with the same evaluator that enforces access, who would lose which environment access if the grant were deleted (op delete) or saved with a lower role (op update, with role and extras). The change is applied inside a transaction that is rolled back, so nothing is written and nothing is audited. A grant that is not the user's answers 404 grant_not_found.
post.summary: Preview what removing or changing a user's grant takes away

post.description: Instance authority belongs to a user, never to a team. Setting what is already set changes nothing. Turning it off for the last active instance admin answers 409 last_instance_admin. Answers the user as they now are.
post.summary: Turn instance admin on or off for a user

post.description: For a user who has not yet set a password. The new link replaces the previous one, which stops working at once, and is valid for BAYPLAN_INVITE_TTL. A user who has already set a password answers 409 not_invited; an unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found.
post.summary: Replace a user's invite link

get.description: The git syncs and webhooks that run with the user's permissions, with the environment each acts on and whether it is active or paused because its owner was disabled, deleted or no longer holds the permission it needs. Empty when they own nothing. An unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found.
get.summary: List the automations a user owns

post.description: Ends every session of the user at once, in the same step that makes the link, and answers a one-time link built like an invite's that lets them choose a new password. It is valid for BAYPLAN_INVITE_TTL (72 hours by default) and replaces any link they held. Bayplan sends no email: the admin hands the link over. A disabled user answers 409 user_disabled; an unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found. Audited as user.password_reset_issued with the number of sessions ended.
post.summary: Issue a password reset link

get.description: For an admin on a user's page. No session is marked current. An unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found.
get.summary: List a user's sessions

post.description: Signs the user out everywhere at once and says how many ended. Nothing is written when they were not signed in anywhere. An unknown or deleted user answers 404 user_not_found. Audited as user.sessions_revoked.
post.summary: End all of a user's sessions

post.description: Clears the lock and the failed sign-in count, audited as auth.unlocked with the caller as actor. A user who is not locked is left alone and nothing is audited. Answers the user as they now are.
post.summary: Unlock a locked user

get.summary: Get the running Bayplan version and source link

get.description: Includes data_not_persisted while the data directory would be lost with the container, and key_backup while the encryption key Bayplan generated into the data directory has not been acknowledged (D-15, D-59). The reverse proxy warnings (the proxy_ ones) are listed while Bayplan has seen that problem in the last hour, one item per kind, naming the newest sighting (D-53). refusal_burst lists, for instance admins only, each user who was refused ten or more times in a minute in the last hour (D-20). backup_failed is listed, for instance admins only, while scheduled backups are on and the newest scheduled run failed; subject is why and since is when the last good backup finished (D-32). unknown_agents is listed, for instance admins only, while agents that were installed after the backup this Bayplan was restored from keep trying; count is how many (D-31). The plain-HTTP warning is the browser's to compute and is not listed.
get.summary: List the instance warnings that need an admin's attention

post.description: Records, once for the whole instance, that the generated encryption key has been backed up, and audits it as warning.acknowledged.
post.summary: Acknowledge the encryption key backup reminder
